intro:
Use a badge to label a state (paid, overdue, building) or a kind (draft, beta, a version number) next to the thing it describes.

A badge is not a control. It cannot be pressed, toggled or removed. For a label that does any of those, use [Chip](/docs/web/components/chip).

examples.title: Statuses
examples.description: `success`, `info`, `warning` and `destructive` are drawn as a tint with text in the same colour, so a column of them reads as states rather than buttons. `dot="pulse"` is for a state that is still changing; use a plain `dot` once it settles.

examples.title: Sizes
examples.description: `sm`, `md` and `lg`. Use `sm` inside a dense table row.

examples.title: With an icon
examples.description: An icon placed before the text is sized to the badge.

notes:
### Choosing a variant

`default` is solid. Keep it for the one badge on a screen that should be seen first. `secondary` and `outline` are for kinds, the four colours for states.

### Reduced motion

The pulse does not run when the reader has asked for reduced motion. The dot stays.
